reuse.why: Holiday handling is threaded through the shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend and a new shared isNonWorkingDay, but the daily-skip versus move decision is re-derived in getNextDate, in a server-only getAdjustedOccurrence and in schedule-template instead of one shared function.

duplication.why: The 'skipWeekend and daily => drop, otherwise move' dispatch exists three times (shared getNextDate, schedules/app.ts getAdjustedOccurrence, schedule-template movesWeekends), and getDatesInRange repeats getUpcomingDates' RSchedule/try/captureBreadcrumb scaffold.

placement.why: isHoliday/isNonWorkingDay and the solve loop sit correctly in shared/schedules.ts, but getAdjustedOccurrence, the occurrence-adjustment rule, is placed in server/schedules/app.ts where the shared layer and budget templates cannot use it.

scope.why: Changes stay on schedule weekend/holiday handling and the new range method for the four steps; release notes and tests are proportionate.

maintainability.why: Any further change to weekend semantics must be made in three diverging places, and schedule-template's movesWeekends || !skipWeekend argument to getNextDate is hard to reason about.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/budget/schedule-template.ts computes its own movesWeekends and drives getNextDate's noSkipWeekend flag with it instead of using a shared adjustment; server/schedules/app.ts getAdjustedOccurrence re-implements getNextDate's daily/move logic rather than sharing it.

disguised_duplication.where: getAdjustedOccurrence (null-for-skipped-daily, else getDateWithSkippedWeekend) restates getNextDate's isKept filter plus frequency !== 'daily' move branch in a reshaped form, and schedule-template's movesWeekends is a third rendering of the same condition.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a daily-frequency filter branch and a frequency !== 'daily' exclusion on its move branch; schedule-template (movesWeekends) and schedules/app.ts getAdjustedOccurrence decide daily-vs-move themselves.
